title: Why So Many Marriages Are Under Attack
paragraphs:
Why So Many Marriages Are Under Attack
The Battle Was Never Just Between Husband and Wife—It Has Always Been About Destroying What God Created to Reveal Christ
There are battles that begin with loud arguments.
Then there are battles that begin with silence.
The kind where two people sleep inches apart but feel separated by miles.
The kind where conversations become transactions.
Where "I love you" quietly turns into "Did you pay the bills?"
Where forgiveness becomes delayed.
Affection becomes awkward.
Prayer disappears.
Smiles become rare.
And somewhere along the way, two people who once couldn't wait to spend forever together slowly begin surviving under the same roof.
The tragedy isn't always divorce.
Sometimes it's two living people burying a marriage one ordinary day at a time.
Maybe that's your story.
Or maybe you're watching it happen to someone you love.
Maybe you've asked yourself...
"Why does marriage seem harder than ever?"
"Why are so many Christian marriages struggling?"
"Why does it feel like the enemy never stops attacking families?"
The Bible answers these questions with remarkable clarity.
Marriage has never simply been about romance.
It has always been about revelation.
From the very beginning, marriage was designed to display something infinitely greater than human happiness.
In Genesis 2:24, the Hebrew text says:
עַל־כֵּן יַעֲזָב־אִישׁ אֶת־אָבִיו וְאֶת־אִמּוֹ וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ וְהָיוּ לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד
'Al-kēn ya'azov ish et aviv ve'et immo vedavaq be'ishto vehayu levasar echad.
A careful translation reads:
"Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and cling (דָּבַק, dabaq) to his wife, and they shall become one flesh."
The Hebrew word דָּבַק (dabaq) means much more than simply staying together.
It means to cling.
To pursue.
To remain firmly attached.
To be inseparable.
It is the same word often used to describe remaining devoted to God Himself.
Marriage was designed as covenant—not convenience.
That is why Satan hates it.
Because every healthy marriage quietly preaches the Gospel.
The apostle Paul later reveals the mystery.
In Ephesians 5:31–32, after quoting Genesis, he writes in Greek:
τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο μέγα ἐστίν· ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω εἰς Χριστὸν καὶ εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.
"To mystērion touto mega estin; egō de legō eis Christon kai eis tēn ekklēsian."
A faithful translation says:
"This mystery is profound, and I am saying that it refers to Christ and the church."
Marriage was never the final destination.
It was always pointing toward Jesus.
A husband sacrificially loving his wife reflects Christ loving His Church.
A wife honoring her husband reflects the Church responding to Christ.
Forgiveness mirrors redemption.
Faithfulness reflects covenant.
Grace echoes Calvary.
When the enemy attacks marriage, he is trying to distort one of God's clearest earthly pictures of the Gospel.
That is why attacks often begin long before anyone notices.
Not always with adultery.
Not always with abuse.
Sometimes with exhaustion.
Busyness.
Pride.
Unforgiveness.
Comparison.
Financial pressure.
Hidden addictions.
Unspoken disappointment.
Tiny compromises repeated for years.
Scripture reminds us in Song of Songs 2:15:
"Catch the foxes for us, the little foxes that spoil the vineyards."
Small sins often destroy what great promises once built.
Many couples pray for God to remove giant mountains while ignoring the little foxes quietly eating the vineyard.
The enemy understands something many believers forget.
If he cannot destroy your faith overnight...
He will attempt to slowly distract it.
Marriage rarely collapses in a single dramatic moment.
It usually weakens through neglected intimacy with God.
Prayer becomes optional.
Scripture becomes occasional.
Church becomes inconvenient.
Repentance becomes uncomfortable.
Then suddenly two people wonder why they feel spiritually distant from each other.
They first became spiritually distant from Christ.
Jesus gave a warning that remains painfully relevant.
In John 15:5, He said:
ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἄμπελος... χωρὶς ἐμοῦ οὐ δύνασθε ποιεῖν οὐδέν.
"Egō eimi hē ampelos... chōris emou ou dynasthe poiein ouden."
"I am the vine... apart from Me you can do nothing."
Nothing includes marriage.
No communication strategy can replace abiding in Christ.
No counseling method can substitute for daily surrender to Him.
Healthy marriages are not built merely by compatibility.
They are sustained by continual dependence upon Jesus.

That does not mean every hardship is caused by personal sin. Scripture also teaches that believers face trials in a fallen world, and spiritual warfare is real (Ephesians 6:10–18). Some marriages endure suffering through illness, grief, persecution, or circumstances beyond either spouse's control. Yet in every situation, Christ remains faithful, and His grace is sufficient.
Perhaps today you feel ashamed.
You've said words you wish you could take back.
You've ignored each other.
You've wounded each other.
You've grown cold.
Maybe your marriage already feels beyond repair.
The Gospel was written for moments exactly like this.
Because Christianity is not built upon people who never failed.
It is built upon a Savior who never stopped pursuing failures.
Peter denied Jesus.
David committed adultery and murder.
The Samaritan woman carried a shattered relational history.
Yet Jesus met broken people with both truth and grace, calling them to repentance and offering new life.
Repentance is not pretending nothing happened.
It is agreeing with God about sin, turning from it, and trusting Christ to transform us by His Spirit.
Grace never excuses sin.
Grace rescues sinners.
Romans 5:8 reminds us:
"But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us."
Notice...
Christ didn't wait until we deserved Him.
He came while we were still broken.
That changes everything.
If Jesus can redeem rebellious sinners...
He can redeem wounded marriages.
If He can restore Peter...
He can restore trust.
If He can transform Saul into Paul...
He can soften hardened hearts.
No marriage is too complicated for the One who conquered death itself.
Maybe restoration begins today with three simple words.
"I'm sorry."
Maybe it begins with...
"Will you pray with me?"
Maybe it begins with one spouse choosing obedience even before seeing immediate change.
That is not weakness.
That is faith.
If someone came to your mind while reading this, don't ignore that nudge. Sometimes one faithful act of sharing God's truth becomes part of His answer to someone else's prayer.

One day every earthly marriage will end, but the eternal marriage between Christ and His redeemed people will never be broken. Every Christian marriage, with all its joys and struggles, points forward to that coming day when the Bridegroom will gather His Bride forever.
Until then, keep choosing forgiveness.
Keep choosing truth.
Keep choosing prayer.
Keep choosing Christ.
Because the greatest love story has never been about finding the perfect spouse.
It has always been about being found by the perfect Savior.
The cross proves that what sin tries to destroy, Christ is able to redeem.
